goal: Implement both src/eventstore.py and src/engine.py. Event store requirements are the same as the medium task: durable SQLite optimistic concurrency, global sequence, exact event-ID replay, conflicting reuse, canonical payload, snapshots and restart. DurableEngine(path,specs,capacity) is a SQLite-backed DAG executor: validate duplicate IDs, missing dependencies, cycles, nonpositive capacity/units/max_attempts and units above capacity with InvalidGraph. Reopening with changed specs or capacity also raises InvalidGraph. Persist each task's status, attempts, next_at, lease_until, token and result. Initially tasks are pending. ready(now) returns a deterministic greedy wave of eligible tasks, descending priority then ascending ID, fitting remaining capacity after running leases; dependencies must have succeeded in earlier calls, never merely be in the same wave. claim(task_id,now,lease_seconds) atomically reserves capacity, increments attempts, and returns a unique token; reject nonready tasks and nonpositive leases. complete and fail require the live token and time strictly before lease_until, otherwise raise StaleLease. complete marks succeeded and stores result. fail requeues with next_at=now+2**(attempts-1) when attempts remain; otherwise marks failed and transitively blocks dependents. ready(now) expires leases at or after lease_until and treats expiration like failure, with the same retry/backoff or terminal propagation. Restart preserves state and live leases. Two independent connections cannot both claim a task. Keep public APIs and do not edit tests.
criteria: The event store passes durable concurrency, replay and snapshot checks
The DAG engine validates graphs and schedules deterministically within capacity
Leases, retries, backoff, stale tokens and terminal propagation behave correctly
Pipeline state and audit events survive process restart
